title: Investigators need to find the answers
article: It will take some time for the province's Special Investigations Unit to complete its examination of the shooting death of a Hammond, Ont., man by the Ontario Provincial Police.
Until that investigation is released, it is both premature and inappropriate to draw any conclusions.
But that doesn't mean some questions shouldn't be raised, with the expectation that they will be addressed, whether through the SIU report or through procedures such as an inquest.
Right now, we know little about what happened.
According to press releases from the SIU and the OPP, officers from the Leeds County OPP detachment were conducting a RIDE program on the Highway 401 off-ramp at Stewart Boulevard on Friday night.

The driver of a pickup truck - identified Tuesday as Phillip Jeffrey Charbonneau, 35 - spoke to officers and then fled the scene, leading to a police chase up Stewart Boulevard, which turns into County Road 29 at the city limits.
At Forthton, the suspect vehicle and police cruisers collided, an officer was struck, and officers shot the man dead.
Two officers were treated for minor injuries.
As is common in such cases, the police say nothing upon the point the SIU begins investigating.
And the SIU is not known for being forthcoming, either.
It took four days for them even to release the name of the deceased.
The difficulty with such cases is that the only witnesses are generally the officers themselves, and they are frequently hesitant to talk to SIU investigators.
In this case, however, there is at least one eyewitness to at least part of the incident.
Julie Young watched it unfold from her apartment window, above the Cedar Valley Golf and Country Club.
Astonishingly, at the time Young spoke to The Recorder and Times on Monday she had not been approached by investigators.
Surely, an independent civilian witness would be one of the first people investigators should talk to.
As well as the circumstances of the shooting, we hope the SIU probes what led to the chase.
In this case, we need to know why the officers decided to pursue the driver.

If protection of the public is the aim, surely it is imprudent, to say the least, to chase a suspected impaired driver, since the risk rises exponentially if he is driving at high speed trying to evade police.
No one should jump to any conclusions about what happened here.
But eventually, we need to know why the police chased Phillip Jeffrey Charbonneau and why they shot him.
